attempts.text:
<plan>
drive car1 myagang-shelter nilkantha-temple
drive car1 nilkantha-temple naukunda-village
drive car1 naukunda-village galchhi-village
load car1 injured 1
load car1 child 3
drive car1 galchhi-village naukunda-village
drive car1 naukunda-village nilkantha-temple
drive car1 nilkantha-temple myagang-shelter
unload car1 injured 1
unload car1 child 3
drive car2 myagang-shelter nilkantha-temple
load car2 adult 4
drive car2 nilkantha-temple myagang-shelter
unload car2 adult 4
defer nilkantha-temple adult 3
defer bidur-school child 3
defer shivapuri-care-home elderly 4
</plan>
COST: 716

**Basis for the plan:**
- Only Myagang shelter is an evacuation point, since Nilkantha temple is not designated.
- Car1 rescues the Galchhi group (1 injured, 3 children) in a single full load. This costs 214 minutes of driving and avoids 260 in penalties.
- Car2 takes 4 adults from Nilkantha temple (62 minutes, avoiding 80 in penalties). A second adult trip would cost 62 minutes to avoid only 60, so the last 3 adults are deferred.
- Reaching Bidur school and Shivapuri care home requires 238 and 278 minutes of round-trip driving respectively. Those trips avoid less penalty than they cost, so the 3 pupils and 4 frail elderly are deferred. Combining them on one car does not improve the total.

**Concerns for the coordinator:**
- The cost model favours deferral for the 4 elderly at Shivapuri and the 3 pupils at Bidur, but these are vulnerable people who would wait for a later wave. I recommend a human decision-maker review this before it is executed. The optimal plan under the stated penalties may not be the right humanitarian choice.
- The plan depends on the Galchhi–Bidur road staying closed. The Galchhi–Bidur route is flooded, and the Galchhi and Dhunche routes to Shivapuri are closed by police.
- The 4 adults rescued at Nilkantha temple are taken to Myagang shelter, which has capacity for them, but this should be confirmed by the shelter.
